description: HuggingFace Text Generation Inference server. Docker-compose-first LLM serving with HF's production Rust/Python server — continuous batching, Flash Attention 2, quantization (AWQ, GPTQ, EETQ, bitsandbytes), tensor-parallel sharding, and a native /generate + OpenAI-compatible surface. Pulls weights straight from the Hub.

buildHints.whenToUse: Pick TGI when the model lives on the HuggingFace Hub, docker-compose is the preferred deploy surface, and you want HF's production server (continuous batching, Flash Attention, multi-GPU sharding) without writing a FastAPI wrapper. Choose vllm-server instead when you need PagedAttention / custom OpenAI-compat Python glue; choose ollama-server for local GGUF-first workflows.
firstSteps: Copy .env.example to .env and set HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN (required for gated models: Llama, Mistral, Gemma)
Edit MODEL_ID in .env or docker-compose.yml to the HF repo you want to serve
docker compose up -d — first boot pulls weights to the ./data volume (can be 15-60GB)
gotchas: TGI pins a specific transformers version per image tag. Use a fixed tag (e.g. 2.3.1) in production — `latest` can silently break custom architectures.
Gated models (Llama, Mistral, Gemma) require HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN AND acceptance of the model license on the Hub UI — token alone is not enough.
SHM size: the default docker /dev/shm is 64MB which crashes NCCL on multi-GPU. Keep the `shm_size: 1gb` block in docker-compose.yml.
MAX_INPUT_LENGTH must be strictly less than MAX_TOTAL_TOKENS (the difference is the generation budget). TGI refuses to start if they're equal.
Quantization: `--quantize awq` needs AWQ-packed weights; `bitsandbytes-nf4` works on raw weights but is slower. Don't mix.
CUDA: requires the nvidia container toolkit. `docker compose up` with no GPU silently falls back to CPU and OOMs on any non-tiny model.
